I'm mapping out the setup process: pulling and building the required images (which could be time-intensive, especially with the tooling image needing PHP and Node packages, plus the web application image), then running the API setup inside the tooling container to install dependencies and generate the app key, before moving on to the web application setup.

For the web app, I need to handle the schema generation carefully — the dev script calls `generate-schema` which fetches from `http://api/v1_openapi.json` (reachable from within the compose network), so I'll create the `.env.local` with the token first, then either run `npm run dev` or do a full build. I'm planning to run the web app both via dev server on port 3000 and also build the docker image to serve on 3003 for a more complete install. Before building the web app image, I should make sure the `.env.local` exists with the token since the build might reference environment variables, even though Next.js typically only needs `NEXT_PUBLIC_` vars at build time for client bundles.

My approach is to kick off `docker compose up -d --build` to build all four images in parallel, which will pull base images first (php:8.3-cli-alpine, php:8.3-fpm-alpine, node:20-alpine, swagger-ui) — this could take 5-15 minutes. While that's running, I'll check if the database is healthy and verify the FakeDatabaseSeeder exists. I'll run the compose build with `nohup` and tail the log to a file, then poll for completion since each terminal call has a 600-second timeout and the build might exceed that.

For environment variables, I'm setting `USER_ID` and `GROUP_ID` to 1001 (matching the Docker defaults). I'll run the tooling commands non-interactively using `docker compose exec -T tooling bash -lc "..."` to avoid TTY issues. The tooling image should have `nc` available (it's in busybox by default), so the API entrypoint should work fine. Once the compose stack is up, I'll generate a token via tinker, write it to `.env.local` for the web app and `.env` for the API, then start the web dev server in the background and test the login endpoint.

For verification, I need to check the API endpoint returns JSON:API data, verify the Swagger docs at port 3002 load the OpenAPI spec, test the admin panel login at port 3001 (possibly using `php artisan tinker` to confirm credentials), check the web app login page at port 3000, and optionally run PHPUnit tests. I'll also verify the API has the public OpenAPI spec file and check the database migrations and seeding before starting the compose build.
